text: Cascade Outdoor Supply, ticket forty-three-thirty-nine. An AP manager says every invoice for their new supplier, Alpine Trail Gear, defaulted to Net 30 payment terms — but the actual contract is Net 60.

Here's the setup detail that matters: payment terms can live at both the supplier level and the supplier site level, and when a site has its own value, that site-level value wins — it's more specific. So the correct value could exist in one place while invoices default from the other.

Checking both: the supplier record for Alpine Trail Gear correctly shows Net 60. But the specific supplier site used on these invoices has its own payment terms entered — Net 30 — and that's the override Oracle is actually applying. It was likely copied from a template or another supplier during setup and never corrected.

This ticket needs two separate fixes, not one. First, fix the setup — correct the site's payment terms to Net 60 so new invoices default right. Second, fix the data already affected — because that setup fix only changes future defaults, it does nothing to invoices already entered under the wrong terms. Each of those has to be corrected individually. Skipping that second step is a common mistake; fixing the setup feels like fixing the problem, but every invoice entered before the fix is still wrong until you go back and correct it.

Resolution note: name both actions separately — the setup correction, and the six unpaid invoices individually corrected — plus a recommendation to check other recently added supplier sites for the same mismatch. That's every Payables ticket in this chapter. Up next, chapter three: Receivables and Cash tickets, starting with AR that won't reconcile to GL.
